# agentai

> `agentai` is a Rust library for building LLM agents on top of the `genai` crate. An `Agent` holds a model configuration, calls the model with the conversation history you pass in, runs tools the model asks for, and deserializes the final answer into any Rust type that implements `serde::Deserialize` and `schemars::JsonSchema`. Runs can be awaited or streamed; you own the history.

This guide was written for `agentai` 0.3.0 (schemars 1.x, Rust 1.88+). The crate is pre-1.0 and its API changes between releases, so compare with the version in your `Cargo.toml` and with the CHANGELOG before relying on it.

## Installation

```bash
cargo add agentai
cargo add tokio --features full
cargo add anyhow
cargo add futures-util   # only for streaming (StreamExt)
```

Add `serde` (with `derive`) and `schemars` 1.x (with `derive`) for structured output. Add `async-trait`, `serde`, `serde_json` and `schemars` to write your own tools with `#[toolbox]`, because the code it generates names those crates.

### Feature flags

All features are on by default.

| Feature | Enables |
|---|---|
| `macros` | the `#[toolbox]` attribute (`agentai::tool::toolbox`) |
| `tools-buildin` | `agentai::tool::buildin`: date, time, timezone and location tools (turns on `macros`) |
| `tools-web` | `agentai::tool::web`: Brave web search and URL fetch (turns on `macros`) |
| `mcp-client` | `agentai::tool::mcp`: tools served by an MCP server, over stdio or Streamable HTTP (built on `rmcp`) |
| `tokio` | tokio integrations, such as `AgentStream::print_to_tokio` for writing a stream to a tokio writer |

For a minimal build: `agentai = { version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = ["macros"] }`.

## Creating an agent

`Agent` lives in `agentai::agent` and is re-exported as `agentai::Agent`. Every constructor takes the system prompt as its last argument. Then set the model with `.with_model(..)` (required, either on the agent or on each run) and, if the agent uses tools, the toolbox with `.with_toolbox(..)`. The constructors return `Result<Agent, AgentError>` (`AgentError::ClientInit`), because building the LLM client can fail.

```rust
use agentai::{Agent, Provider};

// 1. Provider picked from the model name (gpt-* OpenAI, claude-* Anthropic,
//    gemini-* Gemini, ...). The API key is read from the provider's usual
//    environment variable (for example OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
let agent = Agent::new("You are a useful assistant")?.with_model("gpt-4o");

// 2. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, GitHub Models, OpenRouter,
//    LiteLLM, Ollama, ...). Every model name is sent with the OpenAI Chat
//    Completions API to this URL with this key. Names such as
//    "openai/gpt-4.1-mini" or "vendor/model:free" are passed as they are.
let agent = Agent::new_with_url(
    "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/",
    &std::env::var("OPENROUTER_API_KEY")?,
    "You are a useful assistant",
)?;

// 3. One provider with an explicit key. Model names go to that provider as
//    they are. `None` keeps its default endpoint; pass Some(url) to override it.
let agent = Agent::new_with_provider(
    Provider::OpenRouter,
    None,
    &std::env::var("OPENROUTER_API_KEY")?,
    "You are a useful assistant",
)?;
```

`new_with_url(url, key, system)` is the same as `new_with_provider(Provider::OpenAI, Some(url), key, system)`. `Provider` (`#[non_exhaustive]`) has `OpenAI`, `OpenAIResponses`, `Anthropic`, `Gemini`, `Vertex`, `OpenRouter`, `Groq`, `DeepSeek`, `Mistral`, `Xai`, `Cohere`, `Ollama`, `Fireworks`, `Together`, `Nebius`, `Moonshot`, `Zai` and `Aliyun`.

With `Agent::new` you can also pick a provider per model with a `provider::` prefix, for example `open_router::nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free`; the key is then read from the provider's environment variable (`OPEN_ROUTER_API_KEY` for OpenRouter). An agent created with `new_with_url` or `new_with_provider` is bound to one provider.

`Agent` is configuration only: client, system prompt, model, toolbox, iteration limit and `ChatOptions`. It implements `Clone` (cheap: the client and the toolbox are shared) and is `Send + Sync`, so one agent can serve many conversations and tasks at once. It does not remember earlier runs.

Other builder methods: `with_toolbox_arc(Arc<dyn ToolBox>)` for a toolbox you already share, and the getters `model()`, `system()`, `toolbox()`, `max_iterations()`, `chat_options()`.

## Asking a question

```rust
impl Agent {
    pub fn run<D>(&self, prompt: impl IntoPrompt) -> AgentRequest<'_, D, Complete>;
    pub fn run_stream<D>(&self, prompt: impl IntoPrompt) -> AgentRequest<'_, D, Streaming>;
}
```

Both return the same `AgentRequest` builder with the same methods; only the result of `.await` differs (it implements `IntoFuture`, the future is `Send + 'static`). Nothing is sent before it is awaited. Builder methods:

- `.with_history(&history)`: the conversation so far, as `&[Message]`. Default: empty.
- `.with_model(name)`, `.with_toolbox(toolbox)`, `.with_toolbox_arc(arc)`, `.with_max_iterations(n)`, `.with_chat_options(options)`: replace the agent's setting for this run only.
- `.with_options(RunOptions)`: apply a reusable set of overrides (`RunOptions::default().with_model(..).with_max_iterations(..)`, fields left `None` keep the agent's setting).

Every setter in the crate is `with_*` (on `Agent`, `AgentRequest`, `RunOptions`, `ChatOptions`, `Tool`); getters are bare names (`agent.model()`, `agent.max_iterations()`).

Awaiting `run` returns `Result<AgentResult<D>, AgentError>`:

```rust
pub struct AgentResult<D> {
    pub answer: D,                         // the final answer parsed into D
    pub new_messages: Vec<Message>,        // messages added in this run (see History)
    pub usage: Usage,                      // tokens of all model calls of the run together
    pub stop_reason: Option<StopReason>,   // why the model stopped writing the final answer
    pub reasoning_content: Option<String>, // reasoning returned with the final answer, if any
    pub iterations: usize,                 // number of model calls
}
```

- `Usage` has `input_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens` and `total_tokens` (`u64`, `0` when the provider does not report a count).
- `StopReason` is `Completed`, `MaxTokens`, `ToolCall`, `ContentFilter`, `StopSequence` or `Other(String)`.
- The model name is passed to the provider as is, for example `"gpt-4o"`, `"claude-sonnet-4-5"`, `"gemini-2.0-flash"` or, with `new_with_url`, the endpoint's own name such as `"openai/gpt-4.1-mini"`.
- The answer type selects the output mode, so always annotate it: `let result: AgentResult<String> = ...` or `agent.run::<String>(...)`.
- `D` must be `DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema + Send + 'static`.

Complete program:

```rust
use agentai::{Agent, Message, AgentResult};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let base_url = std::env::var("AGENTAI_BASE_URL")?;
    let api_key = std::env::var("AGENTAI_API_KEY")?;
    let model = std::env::var("AGENTAI_MODEL").unwrap_or("nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free".to_string());

    let agent = Agent::new_with_url(&base_url, &api_key, "You are a useful assistant")?.with_model(&model);

    let mut history: Vec<Message> = Vec::new();
    let result: AgentResult<String> = agent.run("Why is the sky blue?").with_history(&history).await?;
    println!("{}", result.answer);
    history.extend(result.new_messages);

    let result: AgentResult<String> = agent.run("Say it in one sentence.").with_history(&history).await?;
    println!("{}", result.answer);
    history.extend(result.new_messages);
    Ok(())
}
```

### Images in the prompt

The prompt is anything that implements `IntoPrompt`: text (`&str`, `String`, `&String` and every other `Into<String>` type), a single `Media`, or a `Prompt` that combines text and media in order. Use a `Prompt` to send images to a model that supports them (vision); `agentai` does not check it, a model without vision support usually answers with an error.

```rust
use agentai::{AgentResult, Media, Prompt};

let prompt = Prompt::text("What is in this picture?")
    .with_image_url("https://example.com/cat.png")          // the provider downloads it
    .with_text("And how does it compare to this one?")
    .with_image_bytes("image/png", &std::fs::read("dog.png")?) // sent base64 encoded
    .with_media(Media::from_url("image/webp", "https://example.com/a?id=1"));
let result: AgentResult<String> = agent.run(prompt).with_history(&history).await?;
```

- `Prompt::new()`, `Prompt::text(text)`, `.with_text(text)`, `.with_media(Media)`, `.with_image_url(url)`, `.with_image_bytes(content_type, bytes)`; read with `.parts()` (`Part::Text` and `Part::Media` only).
- `Media::image_url(url)` guesses the MIME type from the extension (`png`, `jpg`/`jpeg`, `gif`, `webp`, otherwise `image/jpeg`); `Media::from_url(content_type, url)` sets it yourself (Gemini needs the right type). Not every provider accepts URLs; use `Media::from_bytes(content_type, bytes)` (or `Media::from_base64` for data that is already encoded) then. `.with_name(name)` sets a file name, `.is_image()` checks the type.
- The prompt becomes the first message of `result.new_messages`, images included, so follow-up questions in the same history can refer to them. Large images make every later request of the conversation bigger.

### History

You own the conversation history; the agent never stores it.

- Pass it with `.with_history(&history)`. It is only read.
- `result.new_messages` holds only the messages of this run, in order: your prompt, the assistant messages with tool calls, the tool results and the final answer. Append them to continue: `history.extend(result.new_messages)`. This matches `new_messages()` in pydantic-ai.
- The system prompt is not in the history: the agent sends its own with every request. Do not put a system message in the history. The same history can therefore be used with a different agent.
- A failed or cancelled run (an error, or a dropped stream) leaves your history unchanged and never leaves a tool call without a result. You can retry with the same history.
- `Message { role: Role, parts: Vec<Part> }` is an `agentai` type with its own stable JSON format (`Serialize`/`Deserialize`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`), so you can persist, trim or summarize the history however you want and it keeps working across `agentai` upgrades. `Role` is `User`, `Assistant` or `Tool`. `Part` is `Text`, `ToolCall(ToolCall { id, name, arguments })`, `ToolResponse(ToolResponse { call_id, name, content })`, `Reasoning`, `ReasoningSignature`, `Media(Media)` or `ProviderData(ProviderData)`; keep signatures and provider data as they are, providers need them back to continue a conversation with reasoning. Build messages with `Message::user(text)`, `Message::assistant(text)` or `Message::new(role, parts)`; read them with `message.text()` and `message.tool_calls()`. Reset it with `history.clear()`. When trimming, keep an assistant message with tool calls together with its tool results.

### Streaming

```rust
use agentai::{Agent, AgentEvent};
use futures_util::StreamExt;

let mut stream = agent.run_stream::<String>("Tell me a story").with_history(&history).await?;
while let Some(event) = stream.next().await {
    match event? {
        AgentEvent::TextDelta(text) => print!("{text}"),
        AgentEvent::ReasoningDelta(_) => {}
        AgentEvent::ToolCall(call) => println!("[calling {}({})]", call.name, call.arguments),
        AgentEvent::ToolResult { tool, content, is_error, .. } => println!("[{tool}: {content} error={is_error}]"),
        AgentEvent::Finished(result) => history.extend(result.new_messages),
        _ => {} // AgentEvent is #[non_exhaustive]
    }
}
```

- `run_stream` takes the same configuration as `run`. Awaiting it checks the configuration (missing model, schema of `D`) and returns `Result<AgentStream<D>, AgentError>`.
- `AgentStream<D>` is a `Stream<Item = Result<AgentEvent<D>, AgentError>>` that is `Send + 'static`: it can be moved into `tokio::spawn` or returned from a web handler (for example axum server-sent events).
- Every model call of the loop is streamed. Tools run between model calls exactly as in an awaited run.
- Events: `TextDelta(String)`, `ReasoningDelta(String)`, `ToolCall(ToolCall)` (before the tool runs), `ToolResult { call_id, tool, content, is_error }`, and `Finished(AgentResult<D>)`, which is always the last event of a successful run. An error during the run is the last item of the stream.
- Text the model writes before it asks for tools is also streamed as `TextDelta`, so not every delta belongs to the final answer. Use `result.answer` for the final answer.
- Structured output streams too: the deltas are pieces of the JSON, and the answer is parsed at the end.
- `stream.finish().await` reads the remaining events and returns the `AgentResult`.
- `stream.print_to(out).await` writes the run to any `std::io::Write` (`std::io::stdout()`, `std::io::stderr()`, a `File`, a `Vec<u8>`) as it arrives and returns the `AgentResult`: the text as it is streamed, each tool call on its own line (`[tool call] name(args)`), the writer flushed after every piece. `print_to_async(out)` does the same for a `futures::io::AsyncWrite` (runtime-neutral: smol, async-std, ...) and `print_to_tokio(out)` for a `tokio::io::AsyncWrite` (feature `tokio`, on by default).
- These are shortcuts for `stream.listen(listener)` / `stream.listen_async(listener)` with an `agentai::listener::Printer`. Build the printer yourself to choose what is written besides the text (defaults: tool calls on, tool results and reasoning off): `stream.listen(Printer::new(std::io::stderr()).with_tool_results(true).with_reasoning(true)).await?`; `Printer::tokio(out)` for a tokio writer.
- `agentai::listener::EventListener` (`fn on_event(&mut self, event: &RunEvent<'_>) -> Result<(), ListenerError>`) and `AsyncEventListener` (async, `#[async_trait]`) let you show a run anywhere else, for example in a GUI. `RunEvent<'a>` borrows the event and does not depend on the answer type: `TextDelta(&str)`, `ReasoningDelta(&str)`, `ToolCall(&ToolCall)`, `ToolResult { call_id, tool, content, is_error }`, `Finished { new_messages, usage, stop_reason, iterations }`. A listener error (`ListenerError = Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>`, including a failed write) stops the run with `AgentError::Listener`.

  ```rust
  let result: AgentResult<String> = agent.run_stream("Tell me a story").await?.print_to(std::io::stdout()).await?;
  ```
- Dropping the stream cancels the run.

### How a run works

1. The prompt becomes a user message after your history.
2. If `D` is not `String`, a JSON schema of `D` is sent as the response format (see Structured output).
3. The agent calls the model at most `max_iterations` times (5 by default, see Configuration). Each round sends the system prompt, your history, the messages of this run so far and the toolbox's tool definitions, with the run's `ChatOptions`.
   - If a reply was cut off by the token limit, the run fails with `AgentError::MaxTokens { raw }` at once, whatever the reply contains: tool calls in it are not run (their arguments may be incomplete) and a reasoning-only reply does not start another round.
   - If the reply contains tool calls, each call is run through `ToolBox::call_tool`. The assistant message (with any text or reasoning that came with the calls) and the tool results are added to the run's messages, and the loop continues. When a tool returns a recoverable error (`ToolError::is_recoverable()`), its message (`ToolError`'s `Display`) is sent to the model as the tool result instead of stopping the run. A fatal tool error stops the run with `AgentError::Tool`. If the run has no toolbox, the model gets a "tool is not available" result instead.
   - If the reply has only text, all text parts are joined and parsed into `D`.
   - An empty reply starts the next round.
4. If there is still no text answer after `max_iterations` rounds, the run returns `AgentError::MaxIterationsReached(max_iterations)`.

### Errors

A run returns `AgentError` (`agentai::AgentError`, `#[non_exhaustive]`, built with `thiserror`):

- `ClientInit(LlmError)`: the LLM client could not be built (`new`, `new_with_url`, `new_with_provider`).
- `MissingModel`: no model was set on the agent or the run.
- `Llm(LlmError)`: the request to the model failed (network, HTTP status, provider error). `LlmError` has `status() -> Option<u16>`, `is_transient()` and a `Display` message.
- `Schema(String)`: the JSON schema of `D` could not be generated or is not an object.
- `InvalidAnswer { raw, source }`: the final answer could not be parsed into `D`; `raw` is the text of the model.
- `MaxTokens { raw }`: a reply was cut off by the token limit; `raw` is the truncated text (empty when the reply had only reasoning or tool calls, which are not run).
- `MaxIterationsReached(usize)`: no final answer after that many rounds.
- `Tool { tool, source }`: a tool failed with a fatal `ToolError`.

`AgentError::is_transient()` is true for `Llm` errors that may succeed on a retry: HTTP 408, 425, 429 and 5xx, timeouts and connection failures.

```rust
match agent.run::<String>(question).with_history(&history).await {
    Ok(result) => println!("{}", result.answer),
    Err(err) if err.is_transient() => { /* retry later with the same history */ }
    Err(AgentError::InvalidAnswer { raw, .. }) => eprintln!("unexpected answer: {raw}"),
    Err(err) => return Err(err.into()),
}
```

## Configuration

Every constructor returns an agent with the defaults: at most 5 model calls per run (`DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS`) and temperature 0.2 (`DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE`). Change them with the builder methods:

```rust
use agentai::{Agent, ChatOptions, ReasoningEffort, ToolChoice};

let agent = Agent::new("You are a useful assistant")?
    .with_model("gpt-4o")
    .with_max_iterations(10)
    .with_chat_options(
        ChatOptions::default()
            .with_temperature(0.0)
            .with_max_tokens(2000)
            .with_reasoning_effort(ReasoningEffort::Low)
            .with_tool_choice(ToolChoice::Auto),
    );
```

- `with_max_iterations(n)`: maximum model calls in one run. Every reply with tool calls uses one, so raise it for tasks with many tool rounds. `0` makes a run fail at once with `MaxIterationsReached(0)`.
- `with_chat_options(options)`: `ChatOptions` sent with every request. They replace the defaults, including temperature 0.2. For structured output, the run always sets the response format itself.
- `ChatOptions` (`#[non_exhaustive]`, `Default`) has `temperature`, `max_tokens`, `top_p`, `stop_sequences`, `tool_choice` (`ToolChoice::{Auto, None, Required, Tool(name)}`) and `reasoning_effort` (`ReasoningEffort::{Low, Medium, High, Budget(tokens)}`), each with a `with_*` setter.
- `max_iterations()` and `chat_options()` return the current values.
- Any of these can be replaced for a single run, see Asking a question.

## Structured output

Any type that implements `Deserialize` and `JsonSchema` can be the answer type. `agentai` generates its JSON schema with schemars, removes the top-level `$schema` and `title` keys (Gemini rejects them), and asks the model to answer in that format. The reply is then parsed with `serde_json`.

```rust
use agentai::{Agent, AgentResult};
use schemars::JsonSchema;
use serde::Deserialize;

#[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema, Debug)]
struct Answer {
    /// In this field provide your thinking steps
    #[serde(rename = "_thinking")]
    thinking: String,

    /// In this field provide answer
    answer: String,
}

let result: AgentResult<Answer> = agent.run("Why is the sky blue?").await?;
println!("{}", result.answer.answer);
```

Tips:

- Doc comments on fields become field descriptions in the schema, and the model reads them as instructions.
- A first field for reasoning (here `_thinking`) tends to give better answers and helps debugging.
- The model and provider must support JSON-schema response formats. If the reply does not match the type, the run returns `AgentError::InvalidAnswer`.

## Tools

Tools let the model call your code. They are grouped in toolboxes. Everything lives in `agentai::tool`:

- `ToolBox`: a trait with `tools_definitions()` and `call_tool(name, arguments)`.
- `Tool`: a tool definition (`name`, optional `description`, optional JSON `schema`, optional `strict`).
- `ToolResult`: `Result<String, ToolError>`. A tool always returns text for the model.
- `ToolError` (`#[non_exhaustive]`) separates errors the model can fix from errors that end the run. `is_recoverable()` tells them apart.
  - Recoverable, sent to the model as the tool result while the loop continues: `NotFound(String)` (the tool is not in this toolbox), `InvalidArguments(String)` (missing, malformed or invalid arguments), `Failed(String)` (the tool ran but failed in a way the model can react to, such as an HTTP 404).
  - Fatal, the run stops and returns `AgentError::Tool`: `Configuration(String)` (missing API key, server not running, definitions not ready), `Fatal(Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>)` (anything else; build it with `ToolError::fatal(err)`).
- `ToolBoxSet`: combines several toolboxes into one.
- `toolbox`: the attribute macro that writes the `ToolBox` impl for you.

### Writing tools with `#[toolbox]`

Put `#[toolbox]` on an `impl` block and `#[tool]` on each method to expose:

```rust
use agentai::tool::{toolbox, Tool, ToolBox, ToolError, ToolResult};

struct WeatherToolBox {
    default_unit: String,
}

#[toolbox]
impl WeatherToolBox {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { default_unit: "celsius".into() }
    }

    /// Returns the current temperature for a city.
    /// Use it to answer questions like "How warm is it in Paris?".
    #[tool]
    async fn get_temperature(
        &self,
        /// City name, for example "Paris"
        city: String,
    ) -> ToolResult {
        Ok(format!("It is 21 degrees {} in {city}", self.default_unit))
    }

    /// Converts Celsius to Fahrenheit.
    #[tool(name = "celsius_to_fahrenheit")]
    fn convert(
        &self,
        /// Temperature in Celsius
        celsius: f64,
    ) -> ToolResult {
        Ok(format!("{}", celsius * 9.0 / 5.0 + 32.0))
    }
}

let agent = agent.with_toolbox(WeatherToolBox::new());
let result: AgentResult<String> = agent.run("How warm is it in Paris in Fahrenheit?").await?;
```

Rules:

- The tool name is the method name. Override it with `#[tool(name = "...")]`. Names must be unique in the toolbox.
- `#[tool(strict)]` (or `strict = true/false`, combinable as `#[tool(name = "x", strict)]`) marks the definition as strict: providers that support it (OpenAI and compatible APIs) make the model's arguments match the schema exactly. agentai adapts the schema for strict mode: every parameter is listed as required and `additionalProperties` is `false`, so use `Option<T>` for parameters the model may leave out (it then sends `null`). Not every provider or OpenRouter model supports strict tools, so it is opt-in.
- The method's doc comment is the tool description. Parameter doc comments become parameter descriptions. Write them for the model: say when to use the tool and what each argument means.
- Each tool must take `&self` and return `ToolResult`. Both `fn` and `async fn` work.
- Every parameter must implement `serde::Deserialize` and `schemars::JsonSchema`. Attributes on parameters, such as `#[serde(...)]` or `#[schemars(...)]`, are kept.
- Methods without `#[tool]` (constructors, helpers) stay ordinary methods. An `impl` block with no `#[tool]` method does not compile.
- `Tool`, `ToolBox`, `ToolError` and `ToolResult` must be in scope, and your crate must depend on `async-trait`, `serde`, `serde_json` and `schemars`.
- The type must be `Send + Sync + 'static`. The agent stores toolboxes in an `Arc`, so pass them by value (`with_toolbox(tb)`) or share one with `with_toolbox_arc(Arc::new(tb))`.

Error handling in generated toolboxes: if the arguments do not deserialize, the generated code returns `ToolError::InvalidArguments`, so the model can fix them. Errors returned by your method pass through unchanged: return `ToolError::InvalidArguments` or `ToolError::Failed` with a helpful message (for example "unknown city") to let the model retry, or `ToolError::Configuration` / `ToolError::fatal(err)` to stop the run.

### Implementing `ToolBox` by hand

Do this when tools are only known at run time or you need full control over errors. The trait uses `async_trait`.

```rust
use agentai::tool::{Tool, ToolBox, ToolError, ToolResult};
use serde_json::{json, Value};

struct EchoToolBox;

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl ToolBox for EchoToolBox {
    fn tools_definitions(&self) -> Result<Vec<Tool>, ToolError> {
        Ok(vec![Tool::new("echo")
            .with_description("Returns the given text")
            .with_schema(json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": { "text": { "type": "string" } },
                "required": ["text"]
            }))])
    }

    async fn call_tool(&self, tool_name: String, arguments: Value) -> ToolResult {
        match tool_name.as_str() {
            "echo" => match arguments["text"].as_str() {
                Some(text) => Ok(text.to_string()),
                None => Err(ToolError::InvalidArguments("`text` must be a string".into())),
            },
            _ => Err(ToolError::NotFound(tool_name)),
        }
    }
}
```

Build `Tool` with `Tool::new(name)` and its `with_*` methods (`with_description`, `with_schema`, `with_strict`); its `name` is a `String`. Return `ToolError::NotFound` for names you do not handle. `ToolBoxSet` relies on it.

### Combining toolboxes

```rust
use agentai::tool::ToolBoxSet;

let mut tools = ToolBoxSet::new();
tools.add_tool(WebSearchToolBox::new(&brave_api_key));
tools.add_tool(WebFetchToolBox::new());

let agent = agent.with_toolbox(tools);
```

`tools_definitions` joins the definitions of all toolboxes. `call_tool` tries the toolboxes in the order they were added and uses the first one that does not return `NotFound`. If two toolboxes define the same tool name, the first one wins.

## Ready-made toolboxes

### Date, time and location (`tools-buildin`)

```rust
use agentai::tool::buildin::{CurrentDateAndTimeToolBox, LocationToolBox};
```

`CurrentDateAndTimeToolBox {}` gives the model these tools:

- `get_today_date`: today's date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the system's local timezone.
- `get_current_time`: the local time as `HH:MM:SS`.
- `get_current_datetime`: the local date and time in RFC 3339.
- `get_day_of_week(date)`: the weekday of a `YYYY-MM-DD` date.
- `get_time_in_timezone(timezone)`: the current time in an IANA timezone such as `Europe/Warsaw`.
- `convert_time(source_timezone, time, target_timezone)`: converts an `HH:MM` time between IANA timezones.

`LocationToolBox` has `get_location(location)`, which looks up a place or address with the OpenStreetMap Nominatim API and returns its display name, latitude and longitude. Follow the Nominatim usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/

### Web (`tools-web`)

```rust
use agentai::tool::web::{WebFetchToolBox, WebSearchToolBox};

let search = WebSearchToolBox::new(&std::env::var("BRAVE_API_KEY")?); // tool: web_search(query)
let fetch = WebFetchToolBox::new();                                    // tool: web_fetch(url)
```

`web_search` queries the Brave Search API and returns result titles, URLs and descriptions. `web_fetch` downloads a URL and returns the body as text.

### MCP servers (`mcp-client`)

`McpToolBox` exposes all tools of an MCP server. It is built on the official MCP Rust SDK, `rmcp`. It either starts the server as a child process and talks to it over stdio, or connects to a running server over Streamable HTTP.

```rust
use agentai::tool::mcp::McpToolBox;

// command, arguments, optional environment variables (Option<HashMap<String, String>>)
let mcp_tools = McpToolBox::new("uvx", ["mcp-server-time", "--local-timezone", "UTC"], None).await?;

// or a server that is already running
let remote_tools = McpToolBox::new_http("http://localhost:8000/mcp").await?;
// with a bearer token (without the "Bearer " prefix)
let hosted_tools = McpToolBox::new_http_with_bearer("https://example.com/mcp", &token).await?;

// per run, or for every run with agent.with_toolbox(mcp_tools)
let result: AgentResult<String> = agent.run("What time is it in Poland?").with_toolbox(mcp_tools).await?;
```

The server's tool list is read once, when the toolbox is created.

- **Unknown tools:** a tool name the server does not offer returns `ToolError::NotFound`, so an `McpToolBox` can sit anywhere in a `ToolBoxSet`.
- **Tool errors:** when the server reports a tool error (`isError`), the call returns `ToolError::Failed` with the server's message, which the agent passes to the model. A closed or broken transport returns `ToolError::Fatal` and stops the run.
- **Connecting:** `new`, `new_http` and `new_http_with_bearer` return `Result<McpToolBox, ToolError>`; a server that cannot be started or reached is `ToolError::Configuration`.
- **Results:** text blocks of the result are joined with newlines. If there is no text, the structured content is returned as JSON. Images, audio and embedded resources are not forwarded; each becomes a placeholder such as `[image omitted]`.

## Logging

`agentai` logs through the `log` crate: the prompt, each loop round and the answer at `debug`, tool calls and tool results at `trace`. Install any `log` backend (the examples use `simplelog`) to see them.

## Limits in 0.3.0

- Tool results are text only; a tool cannot return an image to the model.
- Only text and tool calls are used from a reply for the answer. Images returned by the model are kept in `new_messages` as `Part::Media` but not in `result.answer`.
- There is no way to plug in a custom LLM client; use `new_with_url` or `new_with_provider`.
